sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and imports
sections.what: Brings in the tools this file needs and states the file's job: enforce rules that new parametric asset data must meet, while legacy models keep their current contract.
sections.why: The header docstring explains that the checks are additive, so older models do not break.
sections.watch_out: The model and part types are imported only for type hints, so they are not loaded at run time.

sections.name: _subjects
sections.title: Building the list of matching subjects
sections.what: Builds the set of labels that identify one part property, once for all instances of the asset and once for this specific component instance. A claim matching either label counts as about this part.
sections.why: Likely reason: a property can be stated for every instance or for one instance, so both forms are accepted.
sections.watch_out: It asserts that the component has an asset key, so calling it without one stops the program.

sections.name: _owned_fact
sections.title: Checking one fact against a part
sections.what: Decides whether one evidence record may set a part property. It must belong to this exact project, match the subject, have no conflicting values from other claims, be eligible, and be source-grade when the property requires it.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the error messages. The apparent intent is to stop unsourced or conflicting values from setting real properties.
sections.watch_out: Source-stated properties need both a source-stated or corroborated truth state and source provenance, so weakening either test lets unsourced values pass.

sections.name: validate_part_evidence (part 1)
sections.title: Collecting competing values per subject
sections.what: Builds a table of every current, applicable claim for each subject and the value it gives. Rejected, unsupported and out-of-project claims are skipped. Numeric values are scaled by the unit factor first so that equal amounts in different units compare as equal.
sections.why: The inline comment says a selected edge cannot hide another current claim, including ones still waiting for review.
sections.watch_out: The unit scaling decides what counts as a conflict, so a change to unit handling changes which values are judged to clash.

summary: Checks that the values of parametric parts and quantities are backed by evidence that belongs to this project, asset and slot, and that does not conflict with other claims.
purpose: Stops the model from accepting part dimensions, positions, materials or quantities that come from the wrong project, the wrong asset, or evidence that is rejected, unsupported or still in conflict.
why: Likely reason: the header says these are additive rules, so older (legacy) models keep their old contract and only new models must meet the stricter checks.
how: First it gathers every current, applicable claim and records the values each subject has been given, so conflicts are visible. Then, for each component with a parametric contract, it treats schedule-authored assemblies (no asset identity) strictly: they may not carry source or measured evidence. The helper `_owned_fact` checks one fact at a time for project match, subject match, conflicts, eligibility and source grade. Lines 121 to 231 were not shown, so the remaining checks are unclear.
inputs: A ProjectModel (the model being checked) and a dictionary of EvidenceRecord facts keyed by id.
outputs: Nothing is returned. When a rule fails, a ValueError with a plain message is raised and the model is not accepted.
risks: A check that is removed or skipped lets unsupported values into the model without any visible sign. The code deliberately prevents omitting parts from turning validation off, so keep that behaviour when changing it.
debug: Read the ValueError message, since each rule has its own wording. Check that the claim's project_id matches the model, that the subject_key matches the asset, slot and property, and that no other current claim gives a different value for the same subject. Lines 121 to 231 need to be read directly before drawing conclusions about them.
